description: The Earth Tiger in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1938 and 1998 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Tiger is the Tiger born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the third animal. It combines the Tiger's courage with Earth's qualities. Earth Tiger years between 1924 and 2044 are 1938 and 1998. The Tiger's fixed element is Wood.

sections.heading: The Earth Tiger personality
paragraphs: The Earth Tiger brings unusual steadiness to an animal famed for impulsiveness. In the five-element cycle Wood controls Earth, and the Tiger's fixed element is Wood, so the animal is said to work on the year element, breaking ground and shaping it to its purposes. Earth Tigers are often described as more practical, patient and realistic than other Tigers, still brave but inclined to plan before charging. They tend to be responsible, fair-minded and dependable in a crisis, with a good sense of what is achievable. The tension between the Tiger's restless drive and Earth's wish for stability can leave them frustrated when progress is slow or when caution seems to cost them an opportunity.

Earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind. Descriptions associate it with reliability, honesty and a talent for holding things together, whether that means a family, a budget or a team in a difficult season. Earth-year people are often portrayed as grounded, fair and good at turning ideas into workable plans. The element is linked with nourishment and care, so it carries a quiet generosity. Its shadow, in most readings, is heaviness: worry, stubbornness and a reluctance to move until every risk has been weighed twice.

sections.heading: Earth Tiger at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

Courage with a plan is the Earth Tiger's signature at work. Tradition casts it as a realistic risk-taker suited to project leadership, property development, operations, policy and coaching, where boldness has to answer to budgets. Before charging it prefers to understand the whole terrain, then it commits completely. Clear objectives and a fair hearing for its proposals keep it engaged for years. Away from the job, the Earth Tiger is protective and steady, more willing than other Tigers to stay put and put down roots. It asks for trust and some independence, perhaps a hobby that is entirely its own. The usual difficulty is pride: having weighed a decision carefully, it can be slow to accept that a partner's hunch might be wiser.

sections.heading: Earth Tiger years and dates
paragraphs: Earth Tiger years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 31, 1938 to February 18, 1939 and from January 28, 1998 to February 15, 1999. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1938 anyone born before Jan 31 is a Fire Ox, not a Earth Tiger. Sixty years separate each Earth Tiger year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Earth Tiger year is Yang, matching the Tiger's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Wu-Yin: Wu is the yang Earth stem and Yin is the Tiger's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Ox year (before January 31, 1938) and the Fire Ox year (before January 28, 1998), and births in the weeks after each Earth Tiger year ends belong to the Earth Rabbit. The new year itself fell on a Monday in 1938 and Wednesday in 1998.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Tiger
paragraphs: Growth for the Earth Tiger usually involves trusting its own boldness. Readings suggest that this combination sometimes over-plans, waiting for certainty that never arrives. Setting deadlines for decisions helps the Tiger's courage break through. Earth Tigers may also take on heavy responsibilities out of duty, so checking whether each obligation still fits is useful. Because they can seem serious, letting playfulness show strengthens relationships. Practical creative work, such as building, cooking or gardening, tends to satisfy both the Tiger's drive and Earth's need for tangible results. Balanced well, Earth Tigers combine daring and judgement in a rare way.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Tiger shares the Tiger's San He trine with the Horse and Dog (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Pig, and its Liu Chong clash with the Monkey. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Tiger years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1938 (from January 31, 1938) and 1998 (from January 28, 1998). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Tiger's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Tiger's fixed element is Wood; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Tiger?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Horse and Dog (San He) and the Pig (Liu He). The Monkey is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Tiger called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Wu-Yin. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Wu, followed by its earthly branch, here Yin for the Tiger, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Tiger different from other Tigers?
faq.answer: All Tigers share courage, independence and magnetic energy. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
